analyst_view.overall: A relegation-zone game on Friday night in Encamp: FC Andorra are 21st with 11 points and four league games without a win, Leganés 16th with 15 after a 3-1 home win over Burgos that coach Luis Carrión hopes ends their slump. Andorra's season has been overshadowed by the 2 November match against Tenerife, suspended after a collision with goalkeeper Jesús Owono that led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel; Owono got a 12-match ban the club won't appeal, and Pau López has kept goal since. Diego Alende is banned after his red card at Almería and the numbers already count him and Owono; new is that one Andorran report saw centre-back Bomba struggling physically in that game, so Manso may be short of both usual centre-backs. Leganés get Montero back from a ban, with Rubén Peña carrying a knock; no referee has been named and I found no match preview yet, so the view rests on the club reports and match reports listed.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already add Alende's ban (+6% on Leganés' goals). I lean slightly higher, about 2.9, because one report (Diari d'Andorra) said centre-back Bomba was clearly struggling physically at Almería, so Andorra could field a makeshift centre-back pair against a Leganés attack with Morata, Millán and Sancris that just scored three; Andorra themselves have scored in most games while conceding 24.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with Andorra taking most of them (5.8): Manso's side press high and keep the ball, while Carrión admitted Leganés spent long spells without it against Burgos and dropped deep. That pattern is already what the numbers expect, and Leganés' recent habit of conceding corners is in the momentum figure (+3.9%), so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards, which already includes both sides' heavy recent booking (+11% and +6.6% momentum); Leganés took three yellows against Burgos and Andorra's Alende was sent off at Almería. No referee has been named yet, and nothing I read suggests a needle beyond a normal relegation fight, so I stay at 6.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, about 18 of them Andorra's, which fits a home side that presses and dominates the ball against a Leganés team that tends to sit back once ahead. Leganés' shots conceded lately are already in the momentum figure (+6.9% on Andorra's side), and I found nothing that changes either side's approach, so I stay at 27.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. In line with my goals lean I add a little, to about 9.9, because Andorra's back line may be patched up again if Bomba is not fit (one report) and Leganés' front three looked sharp in the first half hour against Burgos; Andorra's own recent accuracy is already in momentum (+7.4%).
